title: 1916 Central Asian Revolt (Urkun)
summary: In 1916, during World War I, people of Russian Central Asia revolted against the tsarist call-up of men from the region. Russian forces suppressed the rising with great violence, and many Kyrgyz and Kazakhs fled toward China, many dying in the mountains. The Kyrgyz remember it as Urkun, the exodus.

uncertainty.note: Month-level start and end were not confirmed on opened pages; some sources describe the violence continuing into 1917.

where.modern_name: Lake Issyk-Kul region, Kyrgyzstan (the revolt extended across much of Russian Turkestan)
where.historical_name: Semirech'e region, Russian Turkestan, Russian Empire

importance.justification: Large-scale rising and mass killing in tsarist Central Asia, now central to Kyrgyz and Kazakh historical memory.

audience_note: Describes mass killing, famine and flight of civilians, including children.
